title: Swap a cake in under a pastry display dome and cover it, without touching the cake
instruction: Put the cake where the empty plate is, under the dome, and cover it with the dome. Don't touch the cake.
context: Covering a cake under a glass or plastic cake dome is an everyday kitchen and party chore, and the same move cafe counters make with display domes. The dome hangs and sways from its small knob, the plates have to trade places on the spot, and the dome has to come down square round the cake without the cake being touched, since any touch marks the icing. Revision of board task TK-QTH3SB (robocurve/benchmark-tasks#2318), whose authors did not revise it in time; credited to them.
setup: One fixed layout on the station table (top 0.7475 m; x forward from the arm bases, y to the left). Display spot: x 0.30 m, y 0.10 m. Empty plate: flat glazed ceramic, 250 mm across, 12 mm thick, 0.60 kg, loose, centred on the display spot. Pastry display dome, clear polycarbonate (American Metalcraft LFTD8 size), 206 mm across and 168 mm tall overall: a 20 mm straight skirt, a rounded top on a 103 mm radius, a 30 mm neck 8 mm tall and a 40 mm ball knob; 2.5 mm wall, 0.43 kg; resting rim-down on the empty plate, centred over the spot. Cake plate: the same kind of plate, centred at x 0.30 m, y -0.19 m (a 40 mm gap between the plates' edges). Cake: a 6 x 2.4 in round polystyrene cake dummy (152 mm across, 60 mm tall, as sold for bakery display and cake practice), ballasted to 0.50 kg by a 140 mm steel disc 4 mm thick (0.48 kg) glued under it, its top and side dusted evenly with icing sugar through a sieve before each trial so that any touch leaves a mark; on the cake plate's centre. Nothing else.
scoring: 0 for the whole trial once the cake has been touched: by a hand (any part of a finger, or the gripper body's lower corners, within 4 mm of the cake) or by the dome (its wall, inside or out, or its rim within 1 mm of the cake), or knocked (moved 3 mm or tilted 3 degrees relative to its plate); moving the plate the cake stands on does not count. A touch is never cleared. How the plates and the dome are moved is up to the robot. Otherwise from the final state: 0.25 if the cake's plate is centred within 15 mm of the display spot; 0.5 if also the dome covers the cake (its rim lower than the cake's top, the whole cake inside its wall and under its top, dome tilted under 10 degrees); 1.0 if also the dome's rim rests wholly on the cake's plate (within 2 mm of the plate's top, the dome's centre within 20 mm of the plate's, tilt under 2 degrees). Every positive score needs both hands' fingertips and pad midpoints at least 80 mm from the dome, both plates and the cake, and all four still for the last 1 s (no two positions of a tracked point 1 mm apart). Real trial: the dusted cake is photographed from above and from the front before and after; any finger or dome mark in the sugar, or a hand or the dome seen touching it in the video, scores 0; positions with a ruler and the video.
reset_notes: Put the empty plate back on the display spot with the dome on it, and the cake plate with the cake at its start. Brush the cake dummy clean and dust it again with icing sugar.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The dome's top is five rings of flat panels (within 1.3 mm of the sphere), the knob stacked discs. The cake is a rigid cylinder; a touch is detected geometrically: finger plates sampled 30 points each (16 mm wide at the tip, 68 mm at 60 mm up) within 4 mm, or the dome's wall or rim within 1 mm, as the dusted sugar shows it in a real trial.
